chapter: Trummy Young's band, 52nd Street and the Navy
title: Trummy Young leaves Lunceford and asks Malachi to write for his new band
summary: Inspired by Louis Jordan's success and Lunceford's low pay, Trummy Young wants a trombone-tenor-alto sound and talks a reluctant Malachi into joining.

bands.name: Louis Jordan and His Tympany Five

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Playing in Lionel Hampton's big band

blocks.x: Anyway, we had this band... After about... Almost I guess in the second year, about eighteen months, Trummy Young, who had been the trombone player with Jimmy Lunceford's band, decided to get a band of his own. He had been inspired by Louis Jordan, who had gotten a little band -- he called it the

Tympany Five. And Louis Jordan was hot as the proverbial firecracker, and he was making a whole lot of money. And there were a lot of musicians that were with Jimmy Lunceford who were disenchanted with what he was doing. Because Jimmy Lunceford, from what I understand, was sort of like a schoolmaster. He had this good band, a very disciplined band, and good musicians. But as far as him giving them any money that they rightfully deserved, he didn't seem to be so willing to do that. So he began to lose people like Trummy Young or Willie Smith, all the guys...

Anyway, Trummy, after having met me in Tommy Miles' band that he had been a former member of... Because whenever that band came in town, they'd come around and see Tommy Miles, and I got to know him. When he left Jimmy Lunceford, he came down to see me, and he knew that I was doing some writing and everything. He told me about this idea that he had about getting this little band together. He spoke about a voicing. where he was going to use trombone, tenor and alto. After hearing our little band down there, he felt that I could really get a good sound with that. Trummy always could play unusually high on the trombone...
I was really a little reluctant at first, because I was never one to be over-confident about what I could do. So he just told me, said, 'Man, you can do it. Come on, you won't
regret it." Anyway, he finally talked me into it.
